There seems to be a general agreement that whatever happens moderation transparency is a high priority as it is one of the primary things that has destroyed Reddit.

This sub has no downvoting, no discussion or link posting, no mods, only the ability to comment and up vote. The sub only contains posts removed by the sub moderators. I don't know what you mean by meritocracy--a meritocracy means that the best among us should rule. I assume what you mean by this word is that the content that receives the most votes should be the most visible. I think your assessment is too simplistic. The content on the site is mediated by moderators as it is--in other words, the current system includes both moderator oversight as well as voting. I'm saying that I don't think we should allow users to check moderator authority in subs with an appeal system. That doesn't mean I think the voting system is bad, nor that just because we already have voting, that I should get behind adding more opportunities for voting.

If I understand what you're saying: in order to vote in the /m/ version of the sub, you have to have a certain CCP score from the /v/ version of the sub? Is this correct? In other words, having a high CCP score isn't enough: your contributions to the particular sub have to rate at a certain CCP level before you can vote in the /m/ version in order to appeal content and have it restored? Is that what you're saying?

If that is what you are proposing, I will admit that it's certainly a better approach than going by CCP alone. I can only see this feature really being necessary in a small handful of circumstances, though: evil moderator or power grab. I say this because if power users of that particular sub have to go to the /m/ side to restore content that was deleted, then either a moderator deleted high-scoring content in the first place (because why would poor content be upvoted so highly on appeal if it hadn't been upvoted the first time) or some power users decided to try to force content onto the sub that was against the rules of the sub. So now my thoughts are that the proposed feature is very impractical for such a limited use-value. After all, if power users of the sub had enough strength to restore content on appeal, chances are they had enough strength to upvote content in the first place, which leads me to believe they could successfully start a sub to compete if it really came down to it. In which case, I just don't see why having a duplicate of every sub to host deleted content is necessary.
